Title: 'I am not angry, I am hot,' says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has again stressed that the government's correct term is the Malaysia Unity Government, saying Umno's support was fundamental to its formation.
"I am not angry, I am hot!" Zahid said during his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
Zahid then brandished the agreement on cooperation to form the coalition government in front the over 3,000 delegates, saying it specifically referred to the "Malaysia Unity Government."
"What I said in my policy speech, I want to show the cooperation agreement to form the coalition government known as the Malaysia Unity Government. Where does it mention (Madani)?
"Here it is. The definitions and interpretations. Unless the circumstances and context otherwise require, the following terms or expressions shall have the following meanings; the Cooperation Agreement shall mean this agreement and any subsequent agreement made in relation to the formation and operation of the Malaysia Unity Government," he said.
He also hit out at those challenging Umno to leave the government including an individual he labeled as 'Ceplos'.
"Don't ask us to leave the government. They challenge us, saying, 'Leave the government if you dare.'
"Remember, the Malaysia Unity Government exists because of Umno, you know! The Prime Minister became Prime Minister because of Umno's support, you know!" he said.
Zahid said the original basis for the formation of the government comprised 82 seats from Pakatan Harapan and 30 from Barisan Nasional, giving a total of 112 seats.
He said three MPs who were initially from PKR — Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli, Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad and Wong Chen — had since left the party.
"Although the number of seats supporting the Unity Government now exceeds that figure, simply put, they are additional to the original foundation.
"This is because the parties that have joined now are diverse, comprising 18 parties. If we are asked to leave, logically, the original foundation of 112 seats would no longer exist.
"As such, a new mandate must be obtained," he said, drawing cheers from delegates.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid: Umno will not blindly follow those seeking to dictate its direction
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has taken another swipe at Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, saying the party will not blindly follow those seeking to dictate its political direction.
Zahid made the remark while referring to Anwar, who was in New Delhi, India, for the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit, after the prime minister urged his "students" to learn how 'Madani diplomacy' was being translated on the international stage.
"The Umno General Assembly is not only followed by party members. Outsiders are also interested. That is why I said, no matter how much they hate Umno, they still want to know what is happening at the assembly.
"Even the person in India now... he told us to learn from the teacher. We want to remind the teacher that if the teacher behaves one way, we do not have to follow the same example.
"We like Tamil films, including Bollywood films from India, but we do not follow him. If he is the teacher, we also have a headmaster to teach us," he said while winding up the debate on his policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
Zahid said Umno had its own political independence and leadership to determine the party's direction.
"Umno has its own political freedom to determine our own direction. This house has an owner, and the owners of Umno are its members," he said.
He also accused those attempting to influence the party from the outside of being troublemakers.
Zahid's remarks came a day after he used the term "teacher" in his policy speech when urging Umno leaders to listen to the grievances and concerns of the people.
Earlier, Anwar said in a social media post that his "students" could learn from how 'Madani diplomacy' was being translated into efforts to strengthen Malaysia's standing on the world stage.
He made the remarks after arriving in New Delhi, India, to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid: Dewan Merdeka may witness Umno-BN return to power in 2026/2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi believes Dewan Merdeka could witness the return of Umno and Barisan Nasional (BN) to power as early as 2026 or 2027.
Zahid said the venue, which has hosted the Umno General Assembly for more than four decades, had witnessed some of the party's most difficult moments, including the loss of its two-thirds parliamentary majority in 2008 and the loss of federal power in 2018.
"Whether in early, middle or late 2026 or 2027, this hall will witness Umno and BN back in power," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
He said the Dewan Merdeka had also witnessed past leadership disputes, the banning of Umno and major internal crises that tested the party's survival.
Among the events he cited were the tensions involving Tengku Razaleigh Hamzah and Tun Hussein Onn, the Team A and Team B split, the 1993 Team Wawasan contest and the 1998 crisis that followed.
Zahid said the venue therefore carried a significant place in Umno's history and could once again become the setting for a major political turning point for the party.
He said Umno had endured major setbacks but remained resilient and continued rebuilding its political strength.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Tekad 16' to guide Umno's preparations for GE16, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno has agreed to adopt "Tekad 16" as an official party programme to prepare for the 16th General Election (GE16).
Its president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the initiative would focus on five priorities: strengthening the party, closing ranks, strengthening its election machinery, refining its strategy and reaching out to the people.
"What is our resolve? Tekad 16.
"What is our resolve? T-E-K-A-D: T – Teguhkan Parti (strengthen the party), E – Eratkan Saf (close ranks), K – (strengthen our position in the political field), A – Anjalkan Strategi (refine the strategy), and D – Dekati Rakyat (reach out to the people)," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
Zahid said Tekad 16 would serve as the party's official programme ahead of GE16, providing a framework for its preparations for the election.
He also called for any political cooperation or understanding to be built on mutual respect, honesty and a commitment to the interests of the wider ummah.
"Hopefully, this cooperation or understanding can be built on mutual respect, without betrayal, and with honesty for the benefit of the ummah as a whole," he said.
Zahid said unity did not require political parties to become identical, but required them to be mature enough to find common ground ahead of future elections.
"Unity does not necessarily mean that we become the same. But we must be mature enough to find the points that can unite us in the coming elections, including GE16," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Deal directly with DBKL for trading lots to avoid scams, says Hannah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Traders seeking micro-financing and trading lots are advised to deal directly with Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) rather than third-party agents to avoid falling victim to scams.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said those interested, particularly low-income groups, should approach DBKL officers directly.
"I advise anyone interested to apply, especially those in Kuala Lumpur who are listed under eKasih, to contact DBKL directly.
"Do not go through agents because we do not want them to be scammed.
​"The assistance provided by DBKL is straightforward — apply directly, and if you are on the list, priority will be given," she told reporters when met at the launch of Fiesta Pasar Malam.
The festival was organised by DBKL to empower local hawkers and expand their access to institutional financial support.
Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud said the event followed findings by the Prime Minister's Advisory Committee that most night market traders in the capital relied solely on personal savings.
​"Their ability to sustain their businesses is limited due to restricted funds.
​"Through this initiative, we are introducing them to financing systems offered by various government and private financial institutions to give them direct exposure on how to apply," he said.
​The event brought together 12 financial institutions and government agencies, including Agrobank, Bank Rakyat, Bank Simpanan Nasional (BSN), SME Bank, Tekun Nasional, Mara, AmBank, and Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia (AIM), to process inquiries and assist traders on-site.
Fadlun said the initiative also aimed to support business recovery, with DBKL offering immediate site approvals and access to longer-term financing.
"Today, more than 90 night market and food truck traders representing 65 night market locations across Kuala Lumpur are taking part," he said.
He said slots had also been reserved for 12 underprivileged first-time traders.
​"Furthermore, we are opening up nearly 3,000 vacant trading lots across 65 locations.
"Eligible applicants can receive immediate approval today, with rental rates set at a minimal RM1 per day to encourage business growth," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN can win Pahang with PH or PN, says Wan Rosdy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Cooperation between Barisan Nasional and Pakatan Harapan for the 16th General Election (GE16) could result in BN losing 15 per cent of Malay voter support in Pahang, said Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail.
The Umno vice-president, however, said BN could still win the state if it worked with PH.
"With PH, we could lose 15 per cent of Malay voters, but we could still win," said Wan Rosdy, who is also Pahang menteri besar, in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
Wan Rosdy said Pahang Umno had held three retreats involving himself, fellow Umno leaders and division chiefs to discuss the matter.
"We want to determine the most suitable political alignment.
"There are three options, namely BN with PH, BN with Perikatan Nasional, or BN going solo.
"Interestingly, all three proposals show that BN can win," he said.
The BN-PH cooperation is one of three political alignment options being considered by Pahang Umno for GE16.
Wan Rosdy said BN could also win if it chose to go solo, but such an approach carried a very high risk.
"If we go solo, we can still win, but the risk is very high," he said.
However, he said Pahang Umno had yet to make a final decision on which political alignment to choose.
He said the matter was still being discussed and all relevant information had to be gathered before it was presented to Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
"As of today, the matter is still under discussion. Once all the information has been obtained, my colleagues and I will meet the president for further discussions before making a decision," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid reveals past attempts to pit him against Tok Mat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has revealed that there had been attempts to pit him against his deputy, Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
In his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly, Zahid told Mohamad, popularly known as Tok Mat, that those attempts were now a thing of the past.
"Tok Mat, elok-eloklah jadi timbalan (Tok Mat, be careful in your role as deputy). Sustenance never comes to the wrong address, Tok Mat.
"There are those who want to pit Tok Mat against me. Tok Mat, that was a story from the past. Those who tried to pit us against each other have also repented now," he said, drawing laughter from delegates.
Zahid said Dewan Merdeka, where the assembly was held, had witnessed Umno's victories and defeats, as well as periods of division and unity.
"This hall has witnessed disagreements and unity. It has witnessed tears and resurgence.
"But Dewan Merdeka is not a place for us to lament our fate. Every time we are tested, we regroup, rebuild our strength and chart our own future," he said.
Zahid said the party must remain confident in its identity, direction and timing as it prepared for the challenges ahead.
"Because we know who we are, we know where we want to go, and we also know when the steps need to begin.
"This is the place, here in Dewan Merdeka," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Heli crash: Captain Zainol, Dr Ainul Baraah's remains expected to be buried tomorrow
Article:
SEREMBAN: The remains of pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30, are expected to be brought back to Negeri Sembilan tomorrow for burial at the Senawang Muslim Cemetery (Forest Heights) after Asar prayers.
His father, Bee Sham Ahmad, 59, said that according to the travel itinerary received by the family, the remains are scheduled to depart from Miri Airport in Sarawak at 12.10pm on Malaysia Airlines (MAS) flight MH2575 and are expected to arrive at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) at 2.30pm.
"The remains are expected to arrive at Bandar Baru Senawang Mosque at 4.30 pm before being taken to the Senawang Muslim Cemetery (Forest Heights), where the burial is expected to take place at 5.30pm," he told Bernama today.
Meanwhile, the remains of Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 33, are expected to arrive in Kelantan tomorrow morning.
Her father, Kamarudin Salleh, 69, said that upon arrival from Miri, Sarawak, the remains will be taken directly to Masjid Al Karomah in the Baung Besar subdistrict, Pengkalan Chepa, before being buried at the Sri Kedeper Muslim Cemetery.
"Based on the current schedule, the remains are expected to arrive tomorrow morning before being taken to the mosque for funeral prayers at around noon," he told Bernama when contacted today.
Earlier, Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said the DNA test results for the five victims of the crash had been obtained, with the remains to be handed over to their families today.
The crash on Tuesday claimed the lives of all five people on board the BO-105 helicopter operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace for a Flying Doctor Service (FDS), after it crashed near the end of the Long Lellang STOLport runway at about 3.40pm.
Besides Dr Ainul Baraah and Zainol Afiq, the other victims were assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31, and two nurses, Jessie Paya Jok, 44, and Debra Moset, 40.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Temerloh crash claims fifth victim after teenager dies
Article:
TEMERLOH: The death toll from the 11-vehicle crash at Km 110.3 of the East Coast Expressway (LPT) on Sept 1 has risen to five after another victim died yesterday.
Sebastian Seow Jhen, 18, who was driving a Honda CR-V, died after spending more than 10 days in hospital for injuries sustained in the crash.
His father, Seow Beng Wain, was among the four victims who died at the scene.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron confirmed the teenager's death when contacted today.
The victim's remains were reportedly taken to Selangor for burial.
The
crash
, which occurred at 10.44pm, involved an express bus, a cement tanker lorry and several other vehicles.
Four people were initially killed at the scene, while several others were injured.
Three of the victims — Muhammad Nazatullah Nazmi, Nur Atiqah Sofiya Mohd Kazwandan and Muhammad Armaan Nazeef Mohammad Nazatullah — were from Kuantan, Pahang, while Beng Wain was from Kota Kemuning, Shah Alam, Selangor.
Meanwhile, cement tanker lorry driver Zulkarnain Md Noh, 52, who was also seriously injured in the crash, was charged in hospital yesterday with four counts linked to the deaths of the four victims.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno to hold 'Himpunan Perpaduan Ummah' with Pas to test political cooperation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has given the party's Youth wing a mandate to organise a "Himpunan Perpaduan Ummah" aimed at bringing together one million Muslims as part of efforts to strengthen cooperation with Pas.
Zahid said the presence of Pas leaders at the Umno General Assembly yesterday was a positive signal of growing room for understanding between the two parties.
"This relationship needs to be strengthened, not merely based on political considerations, but for the sake of Muslim unity.
"We will engage in political cooperation with them," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
Zahid said Pas representatives who attended the assembly had expressed their desire for the two parties to work together to organise the Himpunan Perpaduan Ummah.
He then called on delegates to endorse the proposal and gave Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh the mandate to spearhead the initiative.
"Akmal, I give you the mandate. Work well with them and organise roadshows from state to state before culminating in a massive gathering at the national level.
"I ask the entire Youth machinery, including division and state Youth chiefs, with the support of the divisions, Wanita and Puteri, to give full support to the gatherings at state level and carry out political cooperation through this joint movement so that it is organised and continuous," he said.
Zahid said the cooperation could also serve as a test of Pas' loyalty and sincerity, beginning in Terengganu, Kelantan and Kedah.
"Let us test them first in Terengganu, Kelantan and Kedah," he said, drawing cheers from delegates.
He said Perlis would be handled separately, leaving the matter to Perlis Umno chief Datuk Rozabil Abdul Rahman.
Zahid said the proposed cooperation should be built on mutual respect, honesty and a commitment to the interests of the Muslim community.
"Hopefully, we can build this cooperation or understanding on the basis of mutual respect, without betrayal, and with sincerity for the benefit of the ummah as a whole.
"Unity does not necessarily mean that we have to become the same. But we must be mature enough to find common ground that can unite us in the coming elections, including the 16th General Election," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sultan Nazrin calls for capital, climate action, innovation for resilient future
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah has called for capital, climate action and innovation to be brought together in a concerted effort to build a more resilient and sustainable future.
In his royal address titled Building Resilience: The Intersection Between Capital, Climate and Innovation at the 17th SC-OCIS Roundtable, Sultan Nazrin said these three priorities were often discussed separately, despite being closely interconnected and essential to addressing the challenges facing future generations.
"The premise of this roundtable – and I believe it to be the correct one – is that they belong together, and that our future depends upon our ability to unite these three priorities in pursuit of a shared goal," he said at the event held at the Oxford Centre for Islamic Studies, United Kingdom today.
He said the world was increasingly seeing the consequences of treating capital and climate as unrelated concerns.
Citing the work of the late Dr Umer Chapra, Sultan Nazrin said wealth should be regarded as "a trust from God" and warned that pursuing economic growth while neglecting other social objectives could bring short-term gains at the cost of inequality, family breakdown and social unrest.
He said the environment was also a trust that must be protected, stressing that no generation had the right to consume the inheritance of the next.
Sultan Nazrin said recent extreme weather events, including heatwaves and devastating floods, had demonstrated the growing consequences of environmental degradation.
He attributed the escalating climate emergency to "human greed and thoughtlessness", saying humanity had for too long pursued growth for growth's sake.
"Shareholder profits, stock market performance, and GDP (gross domestic product): these are what we measure, what we report on, and how we judge success and progress."
However, he stressed that economic growth remained important, particularly for Malaysia as it continued its path towards high-income status.
He said growth brought increased opportunities and broader horizons for Malaysians, but warned that growth driven by greed could not be regarded as an end in itself.
"Growth alone cannot be our purpose, our driving force as a human race," he said.
As such, he called for economic growth to be aligned with climate action, saying capital and investment must now play a major role in addressing the environmental crisis.
He said governments alone could not finance the transition towards a resilient and sustainable future given the scale of investment required.
"The sums required are vast, beyond the reach of any government acting by itself. Private capital, patiently and wisely deployed, must carry a substantial part of this burden."
He urged the financial community to take a longer-term view, to learn to price risks that unfold across decades rather than quarters, and to recognise that the returns which matter most in the end are those that endure.
Sultan Nazrin also highlighted Islamic finance as a model for responsible and sustainable investment.
"A tradition that binds finance to the real economy, insists that capital serves productive and beneficial ends, shares risk rather than shifting it onto others, and forbids the reckless and the harmful – this is most well suited to the demands of sustainable investment."
He called for greater use of sukuk, waqf-based mechanisms and green and blue financing instruments that prioritise impact over commercial convenience.
"We need the courage to challenge attitudes and priorities, rather than fitting our solutions to the status quo: a financial industry that innovates boldly, and prices climate risk honestly – modelled on Islamic finance.
"Indeed, what much of the world has lately begun to call responsible finance, our own tradition has long regarded simply as finance conducted properly."
On innovation, Sultan Nazrin said human ingenuity had repeatedly demonstrated its ability to address seemingly unsolvable problems.
He pointed to advances in clean energy, efficient agriculture, water management and resilient construction as examples of technologies that could help tackle the climate crisis.
However, he cautioned that innovation must be guided by the right purpose and supported by knowledge.
"What we need is targeted innovation, which is guided by and geared towards behavioural change, as well as technical fixes.
"When innovation is driven by the right purpose, and founded upon deep understanding, we see real change for the better."
Sultan Nazrin cited international efforts to address ozone depletion and acid rain as examples of how scientific research, policy changes and technological innovation could produce positive environmental outcomes.
He also warned that commercial interests must not be allowed to obstruct scientific research or environmental protection.
"We must not, we cannot, allow the pursuit of profit to get in the way of the protection of the planet," he said.
Sultan Nazrin also said that climate recovery would take time and that action could not be delayed simply because the benefits might take decades to become visible.
"The impact of humanity's mistreatment of the planet did not reveal itself straight away, and the impact of our attempts to undo this damage will take even longer to materialise.
"We must be patient. We must respect the planet's own healing process. The positive changes we make today could take decades to manifest: and far from being a reason to delay those changes, this is, absolutely, the best reason we have to act now."
He also placed justice at the centre of the climate discussion, noting that countries and communities that had contributed least to global warming were often among those suffering its consequences most severely.
"The nations of the developing world, many of them young, populous, and rich in promise, did not create the greater part of this crisis, yet they stand the most exposed to it.
"True resilience cannot be built for some while it is denied to others," he said, calling for capital and innovation to reach those most in need rather than being limited to those able to bear the financial cost.
Sultan Nazrin also urged young people to respond to the climate crisis with resolve rather than despair, reminding them that they would inherit the consequences of decisions made by the current generation.
"We act, we build, and we plant, because the act itself is right, whatever the outcome may prove to be."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hannah Yeoh: King has sole power to grant pardons
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The power to grant pardons rests solely with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong as provided for under the Federal Constitution, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said.
She said any further clarification on the matter had already been detailed in a media statement released by the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department.
"I have no authority to discuss or issue statements on behalf of the Pardons Board.
"I can only state that I was present (at the meeting) together with the Attorney-General. That is all," she told reporters when met today at the launch of Fiesta Pasar Malam.
When asked when the Pardons Board would convene its next meeting, Yeoh said members of the board would be notified accordingly.
"We will be informed. When the meeting is convened, that is all I can answer.
"The
absolute power
to grant pardons belongs to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, so we have to wait," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid orders free flights for B40 students from Sabah and Sarawak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abdul Kadir has been directed to ask universities to provide free flight tickets for B40 students from Sabah and Sarawak studying in Peninsular Malaysia.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he had also instructed the menteris besar of Johor, Negri Sembilan, Pahang and Perak, as well as the Melaka Chief Minister, to provide free flight tickets for B40 students from their respective states studying in Sabah and Sarawak.
"That is why we have ministers from Umno. That is what you call a president who takes care of his people," he said.
Zahid, who is also Umno president, said this in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.

Title: Zahid: Ceplos, do not challenge Umno to leave unity government
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has reminded those calling for the party to leave the unity government that Umno played an important role in its formation.
He said any attempt to remove the party from the government should instead be done formally through a vote in the Dewan Rakyat.
"Ceplos... do not challenge Umno to leave the unity government," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
"The unity government was formed because of Umno, you know. The Prime Minister became Prime Minister because of Umno's support," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno must turn Malaysia Blue Agenda into grassroots action, says Wan Rosdy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno must translate its Malaysia Blue Agenda into sustained grassroots efforts to strengthen public confidence ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16), said party vice-president Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail.
He said the agenda, introduced by party president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, would not move forward on its own and required the involvement of all party members.
"The agenda must be translated into action and brought to the grassroots so that the Blue Wave phenomenon that has begun can become a Blue Tsunami across the country.
"We need to build relationships with the people, not only during elections, but all the time," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur here today.
Wan Rosdy said the party also needed to strengthen public trust through tangible service and give people reasons to continue having confidence in Umno.
"Efforts to win the people's hearts must be carried out through work that can be seen, language that resonates with the people and leadership that understands their concerns.
"The people do not want to hear what we say. They want to see what we do for them.
"The Malaysia Blue Agenda should not be seen merely as a colour or slogan. Instead, it must be measured by the party's ability to turn public support and presence into votes and victory," he said.
He said the movement must begin as an idea, develop into a movement, build public confidence and eventually translate into votes and victory at GE16.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fatal Desa Green accident not a hit-and-run, say police
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Police have clarified that a
fatal accident
involving an 81-year-old pedestrian at Desa Green was not a hit-and-run.
The victim, a retiree, died at the scene after she reportedly tripped and fell onto the road in front of a moving Proton Saga in the flat's parking area at 2.20pm on Sept 8.
Northeast district Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Deputy Superintendent Donny John Jubang said initial reports had suggested a hit-and-run, but closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage proved otherwise.
"Based on the CCTV recording obtained, the driver stopped on the left shoulder immediately after the accident and got out to assist the victim," Donny said when contacted today.
"There was no element of a hit-and-run, contrary to the initial information received."
The victim suffered severe head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene. Donny added that the driver, a 60-year-old retiree, was uninjured.
"The driver was subsequently traced and lodged a police report at 10.38pm the same day," Donny said. "The driver has been released on bail, taking into consideration his health condition, including heart disease and hypertension, and his need to make frequent visits to Penang Hospital for treatment."

Title: Zahid warns against challenging Umno to leave unity government
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has warned against challenging the party to leave the unity government.
The deputy prime minister said  any move to remove Umno should instead be followed by a fresh mandate from voters or a no-confidence vote in the Dewan Rakyat.
"Although the current number of seats gives a comfortable majority, that is because additional parties have joined, bringing the total to 18.
"If we are asked to leave, logically, if the original 112 is no longer there, a new mandate should be obtained.
"There are two options. First, obtain a fresh mandate by holding a general election. Second, remove us formally and hold a no-confidence vote in the Dewan Rakyat," he said while winding up the debate on his policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
"If they are brave enough, call it (the next general election) now," he said to shouts from delegates who chants inunison the word "bubar" (dissolve).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Tok Mat proposes Terengganu polls to test political partners' sincerity
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan has proposed that one of the "SG4" states, specifically Terengganu, hold an election to test prospective political partners' sincerity in pursuing cooperation.
He said this would show whether cooperation in the name of Malay-Muslim unity reflected a genuine willingness to share power or merely benefited one side.
"I would like to propose that after Melaka, we test our friends' sincerity. Let us ask one of the SG4 states to hold an election. Hold it in Terengganu.
"I want to see what formula you offer," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
His remarks followed Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's hint at possible cooperation with Pas during his policy speech, when he said the colours would change "
when blue meets green
".
SG4, or State Government 4, is a cooperation platform comprising the four Perikatan Nasional-led states of Kedah, Perlis, Kelantan and Terengganu.
Mohamad said the proposed test would gauge the prospective partners' willingness to share seats fairly, stressing that Umno should not be the only party seeking an understanding.
"We want to test their sincerity. We want to see how far it goes. We should not be the only ones chasing after them," he added.
Mohamad also disagreed with calls by some delegates for Umno to remain in the government until the end of its term, warning that the party might not survive until then.
"I fear our party's own life may end before we even reach the election.
"All sorts of things will be done before the term ends, including attempts to weaken and bury Umno because they see us as a threat," he said.
He, however, left the matter to Zahid's judgement, urging him to negotiate the best possible terms.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Era of single-party government is over, says Tok Mat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The days of a single party forming the government on its own are over, said Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
He said the party must recognise this reality, which formed the basis of president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's proposal to establish political understandings with other parties.
"The era of one party forming the government, in my view, is over.
"Let us not dream that one party can form the government, that Umno can form the government on its own," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
Mohamad said the party must take into account the different political conditions in each state when deciding its approach.
Citing Johor, he said strong "Bangsa Johor" sentiment had been reinforced by the state government's performance under Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi.
"My reading, and that of our headquarters, is that there is a major wave in Johor, the Bangsa Johor wave.
"That wave is very strong and is supported by the very good performance of the Johor government under the menteri besar's leadership."
Mohamad said Zahid's presidential briefing and policy speech at the general assembly had outlined Umno's direction and preparations to lead the federal government after the 16th General Election (GE16).
He said Zahid had also set out the framework for the government Umno intended to offer voters and urged delegates to explain it to members in their respective divisions.
"Let us return to our divisions and explain this clearly to our members.
"Our members can then explain it to the grassroots, who are always eager for explanations and facts from us," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Tok Mat: Umno must rebuild its strength as others seek its downfall
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan has reiterated his call for the party to build its own strength, warning that other parties want to see its downfall.
He said Umno could not rely on others to help it regain its strength and must learn from past disappointments.
"Do not dream in broad daylight, because not a single party wants to see us rise again. They all want to see us buried," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
Without naming any party, he said many had sought to bring about Umno's downfall, only to end up in disarray themselves.
"But those who wanted to do so, Datuk Seri President, ended up reading their own last rites. Look at them now, in disarray and fighting among themselves."
Mohamad said a strong Umno would be better equipped to face challenges and prevent others from exploiting its perceived weakness.
"We have experienced what it is like to be let down. So, let us not be disappointed repeatedly.
"Although the president has spoken of political understanding, let it remain an understanding. Do not get so carried away that we forget our priority is to build our own strength."
He urged delegates to prepare their election machinery and called on Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh to keep the party united and negotiate carefully ahead of the state election.
"Negotiate properly. If it is not right, do not proceed. We have dignity. Do not sacrifice our dignity to gain power.
"Umno has never depended on the goodwill of others. It was not founded through the goodwill of others. It was founded because we wanted to defend the Malays, our race and our religion," he added.
Melaka is edging closer to a state election after Rauf hinted yesterday that the state assembly could be dissolved by the end of this month.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Khaled warns of cognitive warfare threats
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Defence Ministry is stepping up efforts to counter growing cognitive warfare threats, including disinformation, digital propaganda and the use of artificial intelligence to influence how Malaysians think and act.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said such threats were no longer confined to conventional warfare but had evolved into hybrid forms that could exploit technology and social divisions.
"Cognitive warfare is a planned strategy to influence the way people think, assess information, make decisions and act.
"All this is done systematically through disinformation and hoaxes, digital propaganda, exploitation of algorithms and psychological operations," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
The Umno vice-president said there were already efforts to systematically use artificial intelligence and other advanced technologies to influence public opinion and behaviour.
The objective, he said, was to create social instability, deepen polarisation and trigger divisions and disharmony within society.
Khaled said such threats were particularly concerning because they could also be used to erode national identity and fuel religious and racial tensions.
"The Defence Ministry is very concerned about this and is doing its best to develop an integrated strategy to face this extraordinary threat," he said.
He said the ministry's focus included strengthening what he called "people's resilience" so Malaysians would be less vulnerable to manipulation and attempts to divide society.
Khaled said a resilient population was an important element of credible deterrence and could serve as a strong line of defence when the country faced security threats.
He cited Iran and Ukraine as examples of countries where people had remained resilient and difficult to divide despite coming under attack.
Khaled said Umno, as a political party, also had a role to play in strengthening national resilience by promoting mature, rational and non-extreme politics.
"We must practise mature politics. Politics that is rational, not emotional and not extreme," he said.
He said every Umno leader was also a community leader and therefore had a responsibility to prevent members of society from becoming easily influenced by divisive propaganda.
"People's resilience is ultimately about our ability to remain united and not be extreme or easily influenced by propaganda that divides us.
"Most importantly, it is about patriotism and our willingness to help the country when needed," he said.
Khaled said Umno would support the Armed Forces in efforts to strengthen national resilience and ensure the country was prepared to face threats in whatever form they might take.
He said controlling political instability and strengthening public resilience were also important to Malaysia's broader national security.
"Umno will not allow this cognitive threat to undermine the identity, thinking and actions of the Malay community and Malaysian society," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malays should learn from Chinese political unity, says Khaled
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malays should learn from the way the Chinese community works together politically despite belonging to different parties, said Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin.
Khaled said Chinese political groups might disagree and engage in fierce political debate, but remained united when issues affecting the community's long-term interests arose.
"There is one important characteristic that needs our attention.
"They may be in different political parties, but they never focus on their differences," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
Khaled said this approach had enabled different Chinese political groups to maintain a common position on issues they regarded as important to the community.
"They may argue with one another, but they do not truly split," he said.
He cited issues including Chinese schools, recognition of the Unified Examination Certificate (UEC) and the interests of Kampung Baru as examples of areas where Chinese groups continued to speak collectively.
"When there is an issue involving the future and interests of the Chinese community, some will shout and some will speak quietly. But they will not stop speaking together.
"This is their strength," he said.
Khaled said Malays should adopt a similar approach by working together on issues affecting the community even when they belonged to different political parties.
He said Malay political fragmentation had weakened the community's political position and made it harder to advance shared interests.
He said Malay unity should not require everyone to abandon their respective political identities, but should allow them to come together when common interests were at stake.
Khaled said mechanisms such as Rumah Bangsa, Musyawarah Nasional and Tafahum Siyasi could provide platforms for such cooperation.
He said the objective was to build a stronger and more cohesive Malay political voice while respecting differences in ideology and political affiliation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno to decide on proposal to raise Puteri membership age limit after GE16
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno will decide on a proposal to raise the age limit for Puteri Umno membership only after the 16th General Election (GE16), said party vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin.
Khaled, who chairs the party's Constitution and Rules Committee, said the proposal required careful consideration as any change would affect not only Puteri Umno but also Wanita Umno and the party as a whole.
He said the proposal had received strong support from Puteri Umno, but the party needed to assess its wider implications before making a decision.
"This is an issue that is not easy to decide.
"The proposal must be looked at as a whole because it does not only bring changes to Puteri, but will also have an impact on Wanita and, of course, the party as a whole," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
Khaled said the committee had therefore decided to defer a decision on the proposal until after GE16.
He said this would allow the party and its wings to focus fully on preparations for the next general election.
"For that reason, the party has decided to make a decision on the proposal after the next general election.
"This is because we want to ensure that everyone gives their full attention and focus to the effort to win the election," he said.
It was reported that Puteri Umno chief Datuk Nurul Amal Mohd Fauzi had proposed raising the wing's membership age limit to 40 from the current 35.
The proposal was among several motions received by the Constitution and Rules Committee this year.
Khaled said the party appreciated Puteri Umno's efforts to strengthen the wing and recognised its importance to Umno's future.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah tourism players seek package tour subsidies
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah tourism players have urged the government to introduce targeted package tour subsidies to help offset airfares between Kuala Lumpur and Kota Kinabalu ahead of Visit Sabah Year 2027.
They said the targeted approach would cushion packaged tour costs without broadly subsidising airfares, ensuring support reaches operators driving arrivals into the state.
They also urged closer coordination with the Sabah Water Department, Kota Kinabalu City Hall and authorities to give hotel operators notice of water supply disruptions, after at least 10 hotels in Kota Kinabalu were recently affected.
They called for long-term planning around fuel pricing and consideration of bringing licensed tourism transport operators into the subsidised diesel control system scheme.
They urged authorities to intensify enforcement against illegal van operations.
They called for a review of subsidised diesel leakage for unauthorised commercial use and support for licensed operators to ensure safe, insured and regulated transport remains viable.
The illegal van operators can undercut the tourism industry by using Budi diesel meant for other purposes, including the reported use of the 400-litre Budi diesel allocation.
They urged licensing and local authorities to regulate unlicensed short-term rental accommodation mushrooming across Sabah to ensure visitor safety and confidence.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar, Modi discuss expanding Malaysia-India ties in semiconductor sector
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi have discussed expanding bilateral cooperation in strategic sectors, particularly the semiconductor industry.
Anwar, who is also the finance minister, said Malaysia and India possess complementary strengths that could be harnessed through industrial cooperation, supply chain integration, talent development, and bilateral investment.
"I also raised the need to facilitate and expedite the entry of Malaysian exports into the Indian market, creating greater opportunities for Malaysian companies to tap into India's large and rapidly growing market," Anwar said in a Facebook post today.
"God willing, Malaysia and India will continue to strengthen this mutually beneficial friendship for the prosperity of the peoples of both countries," he added.
Anwar met Modi at Hyderabad House in New Delhi after arriving in India with the Malaysian delegation last night.
He expressed appreciation for the special hospitality extended to the delegation since its arrival in the Indian capital.
Anwar is in India to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit.
During his visit, he is also scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, and Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.
The summit, themed "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability", will focus on strengthening economic cooperation and advancing trade and investment reforms.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lack of political will prolonging Sabah's migrant problem, says ex-CJ Malanjum
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah's long-standing undocumented migrant problem continues because of a lack of political will to implement proposed solutions, says former chief justice Tun Richard Malanjum.
He said numerous proposals had been put forward over the years - from recalling wrongfully issued identity cards to introducing a distinct Sabah identity card, a kad warga asing and a pas sementara Sabah - only to be abandoned.
"What has been missing is not a legal mechanism, it is the will to sit down and build one," he said.
Malanjum, a Sabahan, was speaking at the launch of a book, "Citizenship in Crisis: The Ripple Effect of the Undocumented Migrants in Sabah".
The book, authored by Sessions Court judge Dr Melissa Chia, is based on court cases, notes of proceedings from the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI), archival material from the Sabah Archives and Sabah government, and field interviews.
Malanjum said many foreigners caught up in "Project IC" — which refers to long-standing claims over the illegal issuance of Malaysian identity cards to immigrants in Sabah — were never actually made citizens.
"They stayed and raised families, and now stand before our National Registration Department and our courts, unable to prove who they are," he said, adding that this had created a permanent underclass of stateless children.
He said although the RCI recommended establishing a permanent secretariat to investigate, manage and resolve the problem, it never functioned as intended due to a lack of political will.
Malanjum said the issue was unjust to Sabah, as the entire human, fiscal and social burden was placed on a single state.
He proposed that if the Federation were to regularise any part of this population, it should bear the burden itself.
"Those found eligible for a lawful status should not automatically be concentrated in Sabah, but distributed across the states of Malaysia in proportion to capacity, with the funding to match," he said.
He said freedom of movement under Article 9 of the Federal Constitution cuts both ways, while Sabah retains immigration autonomy under Part VII of the Immigration Act.
Chia recorded two proposals in her book, including a truth and reconciliation commission based on the South African model and an independent tribunal to determine status case by case.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Analysts: Umno-Pas cooperation carries political risks and opportunities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Closer political cooperation between Umno and Pas could offer political gains but also risks, analysts said, as Umno prepares to form a committee to explore cooperation with Pas.
Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said the proposed understanding would allow Umno to keep its options open while assessing whether closer cooperation with Pas was politically viable, including gauging the reactions of its grassroots, Pas and existing political partners.
"Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has clarified that the 'Grand Collaboration' is not a merger but an understanding aimed at avoiding damaging electoral clashes.
"Therefore, it is a serious opening for negotiations, but its significance will depend on whether both parties can agree on candidates, constituencies and their relationships with other political partners," he said when contacted.
Umno and Pas have traditionally competed for Malay-Muslim voters, making closer cooperation between the two parties politically significant.
Earlier, Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the party would form a negotiation committee to explore political cooperation with Pas, following calls by leaders and delegates at the 2026 Umno General Assembly for closer ties.
Tawfik said relations between Umno and Pas leaders had warmed, although trust remained cautious and conditional.
He said reciprocal visits to the parties' assemblies and Zahid's "blue meets green" remark indicated a willingness to reopen political communication.
However, the collapse of the earlier Muafakat Nasional arrangement continued to shape perceptions.
"Umno delegates will want proof that Pas can honour a new agreement, while Pas must also consider its existing relationship with Bersatu and Perikatan Nasional.
"Consequently, a comprehensive alliance remains difficult in the immediate term. A limited electoral understanding, particularly an agreement to avoid three-cornered contests in selected constituencies, is more realistic."
Tawfik said such cooperation could allow both parties to assess each other's sincerity before considering a broader arrangement, while consolidating parts of the Malay vote and preventing support from splitting in marginal constituencies.
"This may improve their chances, especially where three-cornered contests previously benefited their opponents," he said.
However, he said votes could not simply be added together, as some moderate Malay and non-Malay voters might view the partnership as increasingly conservative or exclusively Malay-Muslim.
"This could weaken Barisan Nasional's multiracial appeal and place MCA, MIC and other BN partners in an uncomfortable position," he said.
He added that the pact's electoral value would depend on how it was presented.
"If it is presented as stable and inclusive power-sharing, it may broaden support. If it is framed narrowly around ethnic and religious mobilisation, it could secure the core Malay electorate while losing voters in mixed constituencies," he said.
On the prospects of an Umno-Pas victory in Melaka and significant national gains, Tawfik said BN remained well placed in Melaka, having won 21 of 28 state seats in the 2021 election.
"Cooperation with Pas could further consolidate Malay support and reduce three-cornered contests.
"But significant gains nationally would still depend on disciplined seat negotiations, effective vote transfers and the ability to retain moderate, non-Malay, Sabah and Sarawak voters.
"Therefore, an Umno-Pas pact could strengthen both parties, but it does not automatically guarantee control of Putrajaya."
Meanwhile, geostrategist and Nusantara Academy of Strategic Research senior fellow Professor Dr Azmi Hassan said the sentiment among Umno grassroots was that working with Pas was the only way, as they saw it, to safeguard Malay rights, Islam as the religion of the Federation and the monarchy.
He said trust between Umno grassroots and Pakatan Harapan remained very thin, particularly because DAP was part of the coalition.
"The trust is very thin. So I think that's the reason the blue must meet the green in this particular case," he said, referring to potential cooperation between Umno and Pas.
Asked whether such cooperation could alienate non-Malay voters, Azmi said it would depend on how Umno managed the arrangement.
"They have to demonstrate that they are in the driver's seat, that they are in control, not Pas. So I think that perception is very, very important here," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Development must not come at expense of values, says Melaka Umno delegate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno must prioritise instilling patriotic and moral values among young Malaysians alongside its pursuit of development, a Melaka delegate said.
Alor Gajah Umno division deputy chief Datuk Dr Mustafa Musa said nurturing these values must begin at a young age, with the principles of the Rukun Negara serving as a foundation.
"As we pursue development, we must not forget our customs and good manners. We must not sacrifice the principles of the Rukun Negara," he said when debating the president's policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
Mustafa said stronger moral and religious values were needed among Malay youths, citing concerns over drug addiction, illegal motorcycle racing and promiscuity.
He said Melaka had taken a pragmatic approach by requiring the singing of Negaraku and the state anthem, Melaka Maju Jaya, as well as the recitation of the Rukun Negara pledge, at all federal and state government premises and agencies every Monday at 10am.
"We must start here. If we want to shape good habits, we must start young."
He also urged Melaka voters to maintain their trust in the Umno-led state government, likening it to a shady tree providing shelter for the people.
"Do not cut down this shady tree or prune its green branches, because we may lose what we have while chasing what we cannot get," he said.
He cited the state's "Wakil Rakyat Untuk Rakyat" programme as evidence of the administration's commitment.
Melaka is edging closer to a state election after Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh hinted yesterday that the
state assembly
could be dissolved by the end of this month.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police hunt two men who rammed patrol car to escape inspection in Kajang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are searching for two men who rammed a patrol car and a civilian vehicle to escape an inspection along Jalan Semenyih near the Kajang Prima traffic lights yesterday afternoon.
Kajang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said a mobile patrol vehicle (MPV) attempted to inspect a green Proton Wira at 3.15pm.
"Both men, the driver and passenger, drove off towards Kajang when police tried to obtain their identification documents," he said in a statement today, adding that the suspects hit a Perodua Ativa and the police MPV.
"The police MPV sustained damage to the right front door, but no civilians or police personnel were injured," Naazron said.
He said efforts to identify the suspects were ongoing through CCTV footage, dashcam recordings, and witness statements.
The case is being investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code for obstructing a public servant in discharge of his public functions.
Those with information can contact the investigating officer, Sgt Mohd Azlan Zulkiflee, at 017-316 1138 or the nearest police station.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar, Modi task Ramanan with coordinating Malaysia-India business platform
Article:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Indian counterpart, Narendra Modi, have agreed to task Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan with coordinating efforts to establish a platform connecting the Malaysian and Indian business communities.
The agreement was reached during their meeting today as part of efforts to strengthen Malaysia-India economic ties, expand business networks and create new investment opportunities between the two countries.
Ramanan said the mandate would focus on delivering tangible outcomes, particularly in attracting quality investments and creating more high-value jobs for Malaysians.
"This platform is not merely about connecting the business communities of the two countries. We want every collaboration and investment generated to ultimately translate into job opportunities, skills development and better incomes for Malaysians," he said in a statement.
India has strengths in high-value sectors including technology, the digital economy, semiconductors, professional services and manufacturing, offering significant potential for closer cooperation with Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Home Ministry to announce effective date for citizenship amendments once ready
Article:
KULIM, Sept 12 — The Home Ministry (KDN) will announce the effective date of amendments to citizenship provisions for children born overseas to Malaysian women once all preparations for their implementation have been completed.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the preparations included the relevant documentation, citizenship regulations and an online application system, which would also involve Malaysian representative offices worldwide.
He said the effective date had been determined by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and KDN would announce it once several administrative matters had been finalised.
“At the ministry level (KDN), all preparations have been completed, including the relevant documents and citizenship regulations. We have also obtained confirmation from the Attorney General’s Chambers.
“The preparations also involve setting up the online application system as its implementation will involve Malaysian representative offices around the world,” he told reporters at a meet-and-greet event at his service centre here today.
He said the implementation of the amendments was expected to provide significant relief to Malaysian women or mothers who had been waiting for the citizenship process for their children born overseas.
He said that out of approximately 50,000 outstanding citizenship applications that previously needed to be processed, about 7,000 involved children born overseas to Malaysian mothers.
“Of the 7,000, only hundreds remain undecided as we are still processing the old applications while waiting for the amendments to come into force,” he said.
He said once the amendments came into force and new applications were opened, applications under the category would be processed in accordance with the new provisions.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution said KDN is continuing efforts to resolve the remaining 4,121 citizenship applications out of the original 50,000 outstanding applications, with a target of deciding on all of them this year.
He said the four main categories with the highest number of applications were under Article 15A, Article 15(2), Article 19(1) and Article 30(1) of the Federal Constitution. — Bernama

Title: Zahid says door for Umno-PAS cooperation ‘wide open’, eyes million-strong unity rally ahead of GE16
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — The presence of PAS leaders at this year’s Umno general assembly signals the potential for Malaysia’s two largest Malay-based parties to cooperate again, Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today.
The Umno president said the gesture indicated that the room for friendship between both parties was now wide open and must be further strengthened before the GE16.
“God willing, we will be open for a
tahaluf siyasi
with them,” Zahid said in his winding-up speech.
The Arabic term means political understanding.
PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan led a delegation of his party leaders to the Umno assembly opening yesterday.
Zahid also instructed Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh to work with his counterparts in PAS and gather over a million Malay-Muslims for a mammoth rally he dubbed “Himpunan Perpaduan Ummah”.
“Akmal, I am giving you the mandate. Work with them well. Mobilise roadshows in every state in the days leading to the mammoth rally,” he said.
After the 2018 general election, Umno and PAS entered a short-lived political cooperation called Muafakat Nasional and were part of the federal government led by Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, followed by Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob between March 2020 and October 2022.
The Umno-led Barisan Nasional coalition later switched support to Pakatan Harapan and formed the unity government after the 15th general election in November 2022.
Both Umno and PAS currently govern Negeri Sembilan together, after all parties fell short of securing a simple majority in the recent state polls — a power-sharing arrangement that Zahid’s remarks today suggests he wants to see replicated on a bigger scale ahead of GE16.

Title: Umno’s exit from unity govt would demand fresh mandate, not backroom deal, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today that the party's removal from the unity government would require a fresh mandate to determine the country's next administration.
He said there would be only two options if Umno were asked to leave the government: hold a general election to obtain a fresh mandate, or formally remove the party and hold a vote of no confidence in the Dewan Rakyat.
“If we are asked to leave, logically, the original basis of 112 seats would no longer exist. A new mandate should be obtained.
“There are only two choices. One is to obtain the mandate again by holding a general election. The second is to officially remove us and hold a vote of no confidence in the Dewan Rakyat,” he
said in his closing speech at the Umno general assembly here.
His remarks drew loud chants of “
Bubar!
” – meaning “dissolve” in Malay – from delegates in the hall.
Zahid said the original 112-seat basis comprised 82 seats held by Pakatan Harapan and 30 by Barisan Nasional (BN) before other parties subsequently joined the administration.
He also pointed out that three PKR lawmakers, Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli, Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad and Wong Chen, had since left the party.
Zahid’s remarks came after he criticised cybertroopers loyal to PKR, nicknamed “Ceplos” by Rafizi, who have called for Umno to leave the unity government, challenging them to act on their demands.
“Don't ask us to leave the government. They challenge us, saying, ‘Leave the government if you dare.’ Remember, the Malaysian unity government exists because of Umno, and the prime minister became prime minister because of Umno's support,” he said.
“Do you have the courage? If you do, throw us out quickly. If you do, dissolve quickly,” Zahid said.
He also questioned the use of the term ‘Madani government’, saying the agreement for the administration under Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, was to refer to it as the ‘unity government’.
Zahid then read aloud the definition of a unity government from a piece of paper he was holding, telling his critics to look at the document.
Yesterday, Zahid called for the 16th general election to be held as soon as possible, saying BN should not wait until the last possible moment to seek a fresh mandate from voters.
At the end of his speech, he told delegates that this would be the last general assembly before GE16.

Title: ‘One for you, one for me’: Tok Mat calls for PAS to put its unity talk to the test after Melaka election
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Umno should press for snap elections in one of the four states ruled by Perikatan Nasional to test the sincerity of PAS, Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today.
Mohamad, popularly known as Tok Mat, said the era of one-party rule was over, but Umno should not let other parties take advantage of its generosity in political pacts.
“So, after the Melaka polls, I want to ask the president to test the sincerity of our friends.
“Ask them to hold elections in one of the SG4 states,” the Umno deputy president said, using the initials for the four state governments controlled by PAS — Kelantan, Terengganu, Kedah and Perlis.
“If they are really sincere about uniting the Malays, let us see what formula they would resort to.
“Our choice would be one for you, one for me. So, from the four states, two should be for them, two for us,” said Mohamad in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno assembly today.
Umno-led Barisan Nasional currently governs Negeri Sembilan together with PAS, with the former holding 18 seats and the latter seven.
Mohamad also reminded Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh to negotiate seat distribution with political partners without compromising Umno’s dignity ahead of the next state election.
The current Melaka state assembly’s term expires in December this year, but Ab Rauf has floated the possibility of dissolving it sooner.
“Umno has never relied on the sympathy of other people. So, Umno needs to build its own strength without banking on other parties,” Mohamad said.

Title: RM60,000 versus RM500,000: Penang chief minister says still weighing DAP’s call for equal funding law
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 12 — The Penang government is unlikely to table a proposed law guaranteeing equal constituency development funds (CDF) at the coming state legislative assembly sitting, due to time constraints.
Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said he had instructed the state legal adviser to prepare a draft enactment.
“It was presented at the state exco meeting on Wednesday,” he told reporters at a press conference after presenting the Penang2030 eighth-year report card at Holiday Inn Resort today.
He said the state government needed time to examine its details, adding that an engagement session with stakeholders would also be required.
“We have some more time to deliberate on it,” he said.
Chow was responding to DAP’s recent call for Penang to enact legislation ensuring equal development allocations for all state constituencies.
On September 8, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the party’s central executive committee had resolved to ask the Penang government to introduce the law.
“CDF should be given equally, regardless of the political background of the elected representatives,” Loke said then.
He said the legislation would guarantee fair and equal treatment for all Penang assemblymen, irrespective of political affiliation, and that the same principle should be extended to the federal level and adopted by every state government.
The Penang government currently provides each opposition assemblyman with RM60,000 annually, while government assemblymen receive RM500,000 in yearly constituency allocations.
Last August, Chow said the state would await a decision from DAP’s national leadership before moving ahead with such legislation.
He said Penang had provided allocations to opposition representatives for many years, although they had repeatedly sought higher amounts during state assembly sittings.

Title: Kon Yeow orders excos to clear unfinished Penang2030 projects before he steps down as chief minister
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 12 — Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow has ordered all state executive councillors to identify Penang2030 initiatives under their portfolios that have not been started or completed.
He said the directive was issued several weeks ago, and that he was personally monitoring the outstanding initiatives.
“I have given an order a few weeks ago for every exco to list down things that they have not completed, and I hope that they will take action to complete it.
“I want to hand over Penang nicely to the successor,” he told reporters after presenting the Penang2030 eighth-year report card at the Holiday Inn Resort here today.
Chow said he would seek explanations from state excos overseeing portfolios that had recorded slow progress.
Asked to rate his administration’s performance this term, he gave his standard reply of 70 per cent.
About eight in 10 key Penang2030 targets had either been achieved or were progressing, he said, covering areas including welfare and housing assistance, local government reform, tourism, education, agriculture, entrepreneurship and youth development.
He identified agriculture as one area requiring further improvement.
“Penang has established 384 urban farms, but agricultural productivity remains below the state’s target,” he said during his presentation.
The initial target had been to establish 100 urban farms; once that was achieved, the target was raised to 500, he said.
The state intends to expand technology-assisted methods such as smart agriculture, precision farming and vertical farming, drawing on Penang’s electrical and electronics industry and engineering talent.
Reducing household water consumption was another target the state has struggled to hit.
“If we can cut at least 28 litres, or ideally 55 litres to 220 litres per person per day, that is considered a win for us already,” he said.
He said the national average currently stands at 225 litres per capita daily, against the World Health Organisation’s recommended 165 litres.
“There is still much to be done. There is always much to be done because a government’s job is never done,” Chow said.
“Today is not a celebration. Today is for us to look back so we can orientate ourselves forward more precisely.”
He said several major infrastructure projects would continue beyond 2030, adding that he would leave it to his successor to decide whether existing programmes should be maintained or replaced with new priorities.

Title: Male elephant roaming near Terengganu village caught, now on a banana diet
Article:
KUALA BERANG, Sept 12 — The Terengganu Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) captured a wild male elephant that was roaming in Kampung Kolam, Ajil, near here on Thursday.
Its director, Dennis Ten Choon Yung said the animal, which had a paw print size of 15 inches (0.381 metres), was captured by six Perhilitan members before being tethered at the same location around 5.30 pm.
He said the elephant would be fed banana trunks twice a day by the department staff before being relocated to a suitable location.
On Sept 10, the Hulu Terengganu Wildlife Department office received a report regarding a wild elephant roaming in Kampung Kolam. On the same day, department staff conducted a capture operation and successfully caught the elephant.
“The capture will reduce the residents’ concerns about the safety threat posed by the wild animal involved,” he said in a statement today.
In this regard, he said his team reminded the public not to approach the area to avoid noise that would stress the elephant. — Bernama
*Editor’s note: Perhilitan stands for Jabatan Perlindungan Hidupan Liar dan Taman Negara, the Malay name for the Department of Wildlife and National Parks.

Title: Nurses wanted: Public Service Commission says 400 posts still open despite hiring push
Article:
KUALA KANGSAR, Sept 12 — The Public Service Commission (SPA) has filled more than 1,000 nursing vacancies in the public service to date, with open interviews being conducted to expedite the recruitment process.
Its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Jailani Muhamed Yunus said the move was among its immediate efforts to address the need to fill critical posts, particularly nurses, who are in high demand in the healthcare sector.
“To date, we need more than 1,400 (nurses) and we have already filled more than 1,000. So, we still need several hundred more to be filled urgently.
“These efforts are ongoing from time to time because there are also nursing positions that require candidates to undergo training, and this training takes time,” he told reporters after officiating at the SPA Madani Adopted Village Project Handover Ceremony at Kampung Orang Asli Ulu Chenein here today.
Also present were Department of Orang Asli Development Director-General Muhammad Akmal Ila Ahmad, SPA Secretary Datuk Ikhbal Hanam Mukras and Kampung Orang Asli Ulu Chenein village head Din Alang.
Ahmad Jailani said the open interview and walk-in methods were introduced early this year through several career carnivals organised by SPA nationwide, providing more opportunities for qualified youths to join the public service.
He said candidates with a diploma in nursing could walk in for an interview, while those who had yet to submit an online application could also complete their SPA application at the interview centre before attending the session.
“This is also a breakthrough effort that we have undertaken to expedite the process. If we use the usual process, there may sometimes be delays. Apart from nurses, SPA is also focusing on filling several other critical positions that require urgent recruitment, including Public Health Assistants.
“The demand for nurses is quite high, particularly as the healthcare industry has become increasingly important in the country. Therefore, the target is usually (recruiting) nurses into the public service, as the possibly better offers in the private sector mean that a large proportion of them join (the private sector) rather than the public service,” he said.
Meanwhile, Ahmad Jailani, who is also chairman of the Judicial and Legal Service Commission, said the government did not prevent civil servants from seeking better employment opportunities after completing their contracts but instead, SPA would ensure that succession plans were implemented by continuously recruiting new personnel.
“They have contracts that have been stipulated in their appointments. However, once their contracts expire, they are free. We cannot prevent any government officers from seeking better employment opportunities.
“So, there are no restrictions in this regard and we give them the freedom to do so. Nevertheless, we believe the important thing is the succession plan, and we will find ways to recruit new personnel. I am confident that if we go to places such as Felda Chenein in Lenggong, we can find youths who want to join the service,” he said. — Bernama
*Editor’s note: The initials SPA stand for Suruhanjaya Perkhidmatan Awam, the Public Service Commission’s name in Malay.

Title: Come set up shop in KL, Anwar says to  Ethiopia after decades apart
Article:
NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim extended an invitation to Ethiopia to establish an Embassy in Kuala Lumpur during his bilateral meeting with his counterpart, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.
Malaysia’s reopening of its embassy in Addis Ababa in September 2025, after 43 years, marked significant progress in bilateral relations.
The discussion also touched on the positive momentum generated by reciprocal visits by both leaders. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed visited Malaysia in 2024, while Anwar visited Ethiopia in 2025.
The Prime Minister said it has been agreed that the first Bilateral Consultation will take place in Kuala Lumpur next year to further strengthen cooperation between the two countries.
Other areas of cooperation discussed included halal products, agriculture, food security, pharmaceuticals, digital services, renewable energy and tourism.
Anwar also expressed his appreciation for Ethiopia’s support for Malaysia’s engagement with Brics during the bilateral meeting that took place on the sidelines of the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit here.
Malaysia’s participation in the Summit is in its capacity as a Brics Partner Country, a status it has held since Jan 1, 2025.
Ethiopia, the world’s most populous landlocked country, ranked as Malaysia’s 26th-largest trading partner in the African continent in 2023.
Bilateral trade between Malaysia and Ethiopia stood at RM446.8 million in 2023, with Malaysia’s exports to Ethiopia valued at RM358.6 million, representing a 24.6 per cent increase from the previous year. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Brics is a bloc of major emerging economies that originally comprised Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, but has since expanded to include countries such as Ethiopia, Egypt, Iran and the UAE.

Title: As new law on campus politics takes shape, minister sorts students into two camps — ‘Agree’ and ‘Disagree’
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Discussions are under way with all relevant parties on the drafting of a new law to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA), said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir.
He said several meetings had been held with representatives of the academic community and university administrators, while discussions with other groups, including students, would continue over the coming days.
“I have already met with Student Representative Councils and asked the National Student Representative Council, which represents students from all universities, to organise their own groups, whether Group A or Group B, representing those who agree and disagree, so that we can bring the views together and consider them.
“This is because I want the new law to be comprehensive,” he told reporters while visiting the Media Lounge in conjunction with the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur here today.
He said the new law should not only take into account current needs, but also address the challenges the country may face in the future.
Zambry said this is important as the UUCA, introduced in 1971, covers various aspects of higher education institutions, including the establishment and administration of universities, as well as matters concerning students.
Against this backdrop, he said, changes in the higher education landscape and the current legal framework need to be taken into account when drafting the new law.
“I have said repeatedly that UUCA was introduced 54 years ago. There have obviously been changes, and some may say that it is no longer suitable,” he said.
In August, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government would repeal UUCA in its entirety, with a Bill on the matter to be tabled in Parliament this year.
